# I. CONTEXT

Ituri province is located in the north-east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and shares a long border with Uganda and South Sudan.
For more than two decades, it has been facing a chronic humanitarian crisis linked to armed conflicts and recurrent displacements of populations.
It has an estimated population of more than 8 million inhabitants, among whom are more than one million internally displaced persons.
In September 2018, this province was affected by an Ebola virus disease outbreak that was raging in the neighbouring province of Nord-Kivu.
The health zone of Mongbwalu is one of the 36 health zones of the province of Ituri.
Considered as the starting point of the outbreak, it is located in the territory of Djugu where several armed groups operate.
It is located 70 km from Bunia, the capital of Ituri province, with frequent population movements towards Uganda.
This locality has the particularity of having several work sites that attract populations coming from other territories of the province and from neighbouring provinces.

# II. HISTORY OF THE OUTBREAK

On the date of 05 May 2026, social networks reported a surge of deaths of unknown cause with nearly 50 deaths already recorded in the health zone of Mongbwalu.
After confirmation of this alert, the Chief Medical Officer of the Mongbwalu health zone shared the preliminary investigation report on 09 May 2026.
On 11 May 2026, provincial health authorities organised an emergency meeting and decided to deploy rapid intervention teams to Mongbwalu and to Rwampara, which had reported suspected viral haemorrhagic fever deaths in patients admitted to the Centre médical Evangélique de Rwampara, originating from Mongbwalu.
Investigations conducted on 12 May 2026, simultaneously in the health zones of Mongbwalu and Rwampara by the Rapid Intervention Teams of the Provincial Health Division (DPS) of Ituri, revealed that most suspected patients or deaths had fever, headaches, vomiting, and intense physical asthenia.
Deaths occurred 2 to 3 days after disease onset with a clinical picture of haematemesis, epistaxis or blackish vomiting.
During investigations in the health zone of Rwampara, 20 samples were taken from suspected cases or deaths.
The majority of persons sampled came from the Mongbwalu health zone.
Preliminary tests performed at the Bunia Laboratory were all negative for Zaire Ebola, dengue, Rotavirus, Cholera, Malaria, Yersinia pestis, mpox and COVID-19.
These samples were sent to the Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale (INRB) in Kinshasa for additional testing.
On the date of 14 May 2026, 13 cases of these 20 samples were tested and 8 were found positive for non-Zaire Ebola virus disease at INRB Kinshasa.
On 15 May 2026, sequencing of the positive samples allowed identification of the BUNDIBUGYO strain, which enabled the Minister of Public Health, Hygiene and Social Welfare (MSHPS) to officially declare the 17th outbreak of Ebola virus disease.
Ebola virus disease (Bundibugyo strain), thus marking the 17th outbreak in the country's history
On the date of 17 May 2026, in consultation with member states, the Director-General of WHO deemed that the event occurring in the DRC and Uganda met the definition criteria set out in Article 1 of the IHR, and declared that this constitutes a Public Health Emergency of International Concern while specifying that the risk at the global level is low but high at the regional level.
On 18 May 2026, the Director General of Africa CDC officially declared a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS) under Article 3 of its statutes.
This declaration followed an emergency meeting of the Africa CDC advisory group, which considered that the worsening outbreak constituted an acute risk to continental health security.
Consequently, the continental Incident Management Support Team was activated to provide support to affected and at-risk Member States in response and preparedness.

# II. UPDATE ON THE EPIDEMIOLOGICAL SITUATION

Thirteen (13) new confirmed cases, including 1 case in Nord-Kivu (ZS (health zone) of Katwa) and 12 in Ituri (Rwampara: 3, Bunia: 5, Nyakunde: 3 and Bambu: 1).
A new affected zone in the province of Ituri, namely that of Bambu.
The cumulative total of confirmed cases is 64 cases, including 60 in the DPS Ituri (8 ZS affected) and 4 in Nord-Kivu (3 ZS affected).
Listing of 414 new contacts, including 286 in the ZS of Rwampara and 128 in the ZS of Bambu.
No new confirmed death.
The cumulative total of deaths is 6, including 2 in Nord-Kivu and 4 in Ituri.

# III. RESPONSE ACTIONS

## COORDINATION

• Holding of a coordination meeting chaired by the Deputy Incident Manager, Head of the Provincial Health Division of Nord-Kivu (Beni) and Ituri (Bunia).
• Holding of the partners' mobilisation meeting on alignment with the response plan.
• Elaboration of the provincial operational plan for the Ebola Virus Disease incident in the DPS Ituri and Nord-Kivu.

## EPIDEMIOLOGICAL SURVEILLANCE

Support to the ZS of Katwa and Goma in in-depth investigation and listing of contacts around confirmed cases.
Setting up of an alert management system (popularisation of the civil protection toll-free number).
Start of contact monitoring around the confirmed case of the ZS of Goma and activation underway in the ZS of Ituri.
Alert note from the corresponding PoE of Ntoronko/Uganda on the risk of contamination by Congolese residing in Uganda returning from mourning venues of their deceased brothers in the DRC on the shores of Lake Albert.
In-depth investigations and listing of contacts around 4 confirmed cases in Nord Kivu and 58 cases in Ituri.

## RISK COMMUNICATION AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT (RCCE)

• Dissemination of the message from the Military Governor of the Province on compliance with control measures against the Communication plan currently being drafted
• Production of provisional communication schedules
• Production of two official messages, one for preparedness and the other for response
• Communication session for provincial government cadres and officers during morning roll call;
• Briefing of Presicodesa on strengthening SBC, CREC, alert escalation and community feedback collection;
• Holding of the first meeting for analysis of rumours and community feedback.
• Advocacy with the Mayor of the City of Bunia to prohibit the organisation of funeral wakes during this period of the MVE (Ebola virus disease) response
• Advocacy with the Sous Proved EPST Bunia to cascade the PROVED instruction prohibiting the expulsion of pupils for not wearing masks.
• Advocacy with the Commander of the Régie des Voies Aériennes (RVA) of Bunia

## INFECTION PREVENTION AND CONTROL

ZS Bunia
▪ 2 EDS completed and 1 underway;
▪ Briefing of 5 healthcare providers from the emergency room of HGR (general referral hospital)-Bunia on preventive measures;
▪ Provision of PPE and decontamination equipment for the practical session of ZS Bunia teams;
▪ Decontamination of the isolation building of HGR-Bunia.
▪ Provision of some PCI supplies by the partner ALIMA

ZS Rwampara
▪ Briefing of 4 staff from the BALIDJA Mortuary on wearing PPE before handling any body;
▪ Continuation of briefing of 63 healthcare providers (Hygienists, nurses, Doctors and Midwives) from CME Nyakunde) on biomedical waste management.
▪ 3 EDS completed and 1 underway
▪ Decontamination of the isolation room at HGR/Rwampara;
▪ Briefing of 10 Cleaners and 15 PCI supervisors on donning and doffing PPE.

ZS Mongbwalu
▪ Formative supervision in 4 health facilities including: CS Uponyaji, CS Rwampara, Poste de santé Amani and CS Tchunga (without assessment);

DPS Nord Kivu
• Decontamination of Matanda Hospital where the confirmed case from the ZS of Katwa is staying;
• PCI scorecard assessment of Matanda Hospital: 70,6%;
• Performance of case mapping;
• State of play of the CTE (Ebola treatment centre) to identify PCI supply needs (PPE, DLM, water supply, waste management, patient flow).

## LOGISTICS

• Elaboration of logistics needs assessment for the ZS of Goma, Katwa, Beni, Karisimbi, Mutwanga, Vuhovi, Kalunguta, Kamango, Mabalako, Oicha, Museniene, Kayina, Alimbongo, Butembo;
• Acquisition of Starlink kits for internet connectivity from UNICEF;
• Receipt of 5 vehicles donated by WHO;
• Receipt of 200 litres of Diesel (Support from MEMISA-Belgique).

• Fit-out of a room at HGR Bunia underway.
• Evaluation of the nutritional status of patients in isolation at CME.
• 14 announcements of results;
• Sensitisation of 97 family caregivers, 9 hygienists, 11 labourers, 92 teachers from CSJM and 25 taxi drivers;
• Family meeting with 4 families of deceased persons;

## SECURITY

• The security situation in the city of Bunia (ZS of Bunia and Rwampara) is relatively calm
• Security briefing for deployed teams.

# III. CHALLENGES

Lack of standard CT (transit centre) and CTE
Lack of PCI materials (PPE, DLM, chlorine) in Nord Kivu
Low escalation of alerts by zones;
Insufficient financial resources to support all response pillars;
Difficulty in transporting samples to the Goma and Kinshasa laboratories.
Spread of rumours and proliferation of traditional treatment recipes.
Lack of communication media and tools.
Lack of office supplies and equipment (IT equipment);
Insufficient vehicles for moving teams in the field;

# VI. Recommendation

Operationalise the CT and CTE of Beni, Butembo and Goma (rehabilitation and review of patient flow)
Strengthen surveillance with a view to escalating alerts and tracing contacts never seen and lost to follow-up;
Mobilise resources to support the various response pillars;
Strengthen analysis of rumours and community feedback and carry out actions to address them
Supply communication media and tools
